title: Polity Lec 6
summary: Regulating Act 1773: Governor of Bengal became Governor-General of Bengal (first: Warren Hastings); Supreme Court set up at Calcutta (first CJ: Elijah Impey).
Pitt's India Act 1784 created dual control; the Act of Settlement 1781 rectified the defects of the 1773 Act.

Charter Act 1813: Company monopoly ended except tea and trade with China, Rs 1 lakh for education; 1833: Company became purely administrative, Governor-General of India (Bentinck), Law Commission under Macaulay.
1858: Company abolished, Viceroy (Canning), Secretary of State with a 15-member council; 1861: nomination of Indians, portfolio system, decentralisation.

1892: discussion of budget and right to ask questions; 1909 (Morley-Minto): separate electorate for Muslims, council enlarged from 16 to 60, Minto 'Father of Communal Electorate', S.P. Sinha first Indian in the Executive Council.

1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford): dyarchy in provinces (reserved/transferred), bicameral legislature at the Centre; 1935: provincial autonomy, bicameral legislatures in 6 of 11 provinces, federation never came into being.

States reorganisation: Dhar Commission 1948, JVP Committee, Andhra 1953 (Potti Sriramulu), Fazl Ali Commission, SRA 1956 created 14 states and 6 UTs; Goa liberated 1961 (Operation Vijay), statehood 1987 (56th Amendment).
69th Amendment: Delhi as NCT (Articles 239AA, 239AB); 91st Amendment 2003: Council of Ministers capped at 15% (Delhi 10%); Articles 371 to 371J (371J: Karnataka).
CAG: Articles 148-151, first CAG V. Narahari Rao, reports to the President; Election Commission: Part XV, Articles 324-329, 61st Amendment (voting age 18), multi-member since 1993.

Finance Commission Article 280 (16th: Arvind Panagariya); GST Council Article 279A (Centre 1/3, States 2/3 vote weight, decisions by 3/4); NCSC 338, NCST 338A (89th), NCBC 338B (102nd), Articles 340, 342, 335.
Collegium and Judges Cases (1981, 1993, 1998, 2015); NJAC struck down; categories of NITI Aayog, CIC, NHRC, NCW, CVC, Lokpal (Chairperson + 8 members); CBI is non-statutory.
All India Services Article 312; UPSC/SPSC Part XIV, Articles 315-323; Tribunals Part XIV-A (323A, 323B, 42nd Amendment), L. Chandra Kumar case; 106th Amendment: 33% reservation for women.

Lok Adalat: Legal Services Authorities Act 1987, Article 39A, award final and binding, non-compoundable offences excluded; MGNREGA Article 41; juveniles aged 16-18 tried as adults for heinous offences.
Supreme Court Articles 124-147: 126 acting CJI, 127 ad hoc judges, 129 court of record, 130 seat, 131 original, 132-134 appellate, 136 SLP, 137 review, 141, 142, 143 advisory.
High Courts: Article 226 writs, 222 transfer, retirement age 62 (SC 65); District Judge Article 233 (7 years), 235 control; Nyaya Panchayat, PIL (Bhagwati), judicial activism, ADM Jabalpur.

mcqs.q: Which was the first Act to regulate the affairs of the East India Company, marking the first step of constitutional development in India?
mcqs.e: The Regulating Act 1773 established British government control over the Company.

mcqs.q: Under the Regulating Act 1773, the Governor of Bengal was designated as:
mcqs.e: Bengal gained more power and the Bombay and Madras Presidencies were made subordinate to it.

mcqs.q: Who was the first Governor-General of Bengal?
mcqs.e: Warren Hastings became the first Governor-General of Bengal after the 1773 Act.

mcqs.q: Who became the first Governor-General of India?
mcqs.e: Under the Charter Act 1833 the Governor-General of Bengal became Governor-General of India; Bentinck was the first.

mcqs.q: Which Act made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India?
mcqs.e: The 1833 Act made Bombay and Madras fully subordinate, marking the peak of centralisation.

mcqs.q: The Supreme Court established at Calcutta under the Regulating Act 1773 consisted of:
o: One Chief Justice and three other judges
One Chief Justice and two judges
One Chief Justice and five judges
mcqs.e: Set up in 1774, its first Chief Justice was Elijah Impey.

mcqs.q: Who was the first Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Calcutta?
mcqs.e: Elijah Impey became the first Chief Justice in 1774.

mcqs.q: What system was introduced by Pitt's India Act 1784?
o: Nomination of Indians to the legislative council
Dual control (Court of Directors for commercial affairs, Board of Control for political affairs)
mcqs.e: Commercial affairs stayed with the Court of Directors and political affairs went to the Board of Control; dual control ended in 1858.

mcqs.q: The Act of Settlement 1781 was passed to remove the defects of which Act?
mcqs.e: The Act of Settlement 1781 came between the Acts of 1773 and 1784.

mcqs.q: The Charter Act 1813 ended the trade monopoly of the East India Company except for:
mcqs.e: The 1813 Act retained only the tea and China trade monopoly; these too ended in 1833.

mcqs.q: How much money was set aside for education under the Charter Act 1813?
mcqs.e: The Act also allowed Christian missionaries to come to India.

mcqs.q: What change did the Charter Act 1833 bring in the status of the East India Company?
o: Allowed it only the tea trade
Ended all its commercial functions, making it a purely administrative body
Granted the Company a new monopoly
mcqs.e: The Company was abolished completely only by the Act of 1858.

mcqs.q: Who was the chairman of the first Law Commission set up under the Charter Act 1833?
mcqs.e: India's first (colonial) Law Commission was headed by Lord Macaulay.

mcqs.q: Who was the first Attorney General of India and chairman of the first Law Commission of independent India?
mcqs.e: M.C. Setalvad was the first Attorney General and chaired the first post-independence Law Commission (1955).

mcqs.q: Which Act first associated Indians with the law-making process in India?
mcqs.e: Under the 1861 Act the Viceroy nominated three Indians as non-official members.

mcqs.q: The Government of India Act 1858 is also known as:
o: Act for the Good Government of India
mcqs.e: Passed after the Revolt of 1857, it abolished the East India Company.

mcqs.q: What happened to the East India Company under the Act of 1858?
o: It became only an administrative body
It continued only the tea trade
It was renamed the Council of India
mcqs.e: The Governor-General was henceforth also called the Viceroy.

mcqs.q: Which post was created in Britain by the Act of 1858 for Indian affairs, assisted by a 15-member council?
mcqs.e: The Secretary of State was a member of the British Cabinet, answerable to Parliament for Indian affairs.

mcqs.q: Who was the first Viceroy of India?
mcqs.e: The Revolt of 1857 took place under Canning; he was the last Governor-General and first Viceroy.

mcqs.q: Which commission was set up after the Revolt of 1857 to review the reorganisation of the British Indian Army?
mcqs.e: Queen Victoria was the British monarch at that time.

mcqs.q: Whom did the Viceroy nominate to the legislative council under the Indian Councils Act 1861?
o: Maharajas of Jaipur, Baroda and Mysore
Syed Ahmed Khan, Badruddin Tyabji, M.A. Jinnah
Raja of Benaras, Maharaja of Patiala, Sir Dinkar Rao
mcqs.e: Indians entered the legislative process through the nomination of these three.

mcqs.q: Which system, involving allocation of departments such as Home and Defence, was introduced through the 1861 Act?
mcqs.e: Lord Canning introduced the portfolio system, recognised by the 1861 Act.

mcqs.q: The Indian Councils Act 1861 empowered the Viceroy to issue which of the following during an emergency without the legislative council's concurrence?
mcqs.e: Such ordinances were valid for six months; the Act also began decentralisation.

mcqs.q: Which Act reversed the centralising trend of 1773-1833 and began decentralisation?
mcqs.e: The 1861 Act restored legislative powers to Bombay and Madras.

mcqs.q: Which Act introduced open competition for recruitment to the civil services?
mcqs.e: Lord Cornwallis is called the Father of Civil Services in India.

mcqs.q: Who is known as the 'Father of Civil Services' in India?
mcqs.e: Open competition began in 1853, but Cornwallis is regarded as the father.

mcqs.q: Which Act gave members of the Central Legislative Council the right to discuss the budget and ask questions?
mcqs.e: The 1892 Act allowed budget discussion but not voting on it.

mcqs.q: The Act of 1909 is popularly known as:
mcqs.e: Morley was Secretary of State and Minto the Viceroy; it was an Indian Councils Act, not a Government of India Act.

mcqs.q: The Act of 1909 introduced a separate electorate for which community?
mcqs.e: Under a separate electorate only Muslims could contest and vote for Muslim seats.

mcqs.q: Who is called the 'Father of Communal Electorate' in India?
mcqs.e: Because separate electorates were introduced in 1909 during his tenure.

mcqs.q: The Act of 1909 increased the strength of the Central Legislative Council from:
mcqs.e: The legislative councils were considerably enlarged.

mcqs.q: Who was the first Indian to join the Viceroy's Executive Council?
mcqs.e: S.P. Sinha joined as Law Member following the 1909 Act.

mcqs.q: The Government of India Act 1919 is also known as:
mcqs.e: Montagu was Secretary of State and Chelmsford the Viceroy.

mcqs.q: Which system of government was introduced in the provinces by the Act of 1919?
mcqs.e: Provincial subjects were divided into 'reserved' and 'transferred'.

mcqs.q: Under dyarchy, who administered the 'transferred' subjects?
o: Indian ministers responsible to the legislative council
The Governor and his Executive Council
mcqs.e: Reserved subjects (law and order, finance) stayed with the Governor, who was not responsible to the council.

mcqs.q: What kind of legislature did the Act of 1919 introduce at the Centre?
mcqs.e: It also extended separate electorates to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans.

mcqs.q: Which Act abolished dyarchy in the provinces and granted provincial autonomy?
mcqs.e: The 1935 Act shifted dyarchy to the Centre and gave autonomy to the provinces.

mcqs.q: Under the Act of 1935, how many provinces got bicameral legislatures?
mcqs.e: The remaining provinces had unicameral legislatures.

mcqs.q: Why could the All-India Federation proposed by the Act of 1935 not be established?
o: The princely states did not agree to join
World War II did not happen
mcqs.e: The Act provided for a federation, but the princely states did not give their consent.

mcqs.q: Under the dyarchy of 1919, subjects like education, health and agriculture were:
mcqs.e: Important subjects like law and order and finance were reserved.

mcqs.q: What was the official name of the Rowlatt Act?
mcqs.e: Known as 'no appeal, no vakil, no daleel'; Gandhiji launched the Rowlatt Satyagraha against it.

mcqs.q: The arrest of which leaders during the Rowlatt Satyagraha led to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
o: Lala Lajpat Rai and Bhagat Singh
mcqs.e: The Non-Cooperation Movement followed the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

mcqs.q: Which commission was appointed to examine the formation of states on a linguistic basis?
mcqs.e: The Dhar Commission (1948) recommended administrative convenience rather than language as the basis.

mcqs.q: The Sarkaria Commission was related to:
mcqs.e: Set up in 1983; on its recommendation the first Inter-State Council was formed in 1990.

mcqs.q: Which committee was set up in 1976 for Fundamental Duties?
mcqs.e: Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976.

mcqs.q: Who were the members of the JVP Committee (1948)?
o: Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel, Pattabhi Sitaramayya
mcqs.e: It too rejected language as the basis for reorganising states.

mcqs.q: Which was the first linguistic state of India?
mcqs.e: Andhra State was formed in 1953 after Potti Sriramulu died during his fast unto death.

mcqs.q: Who were the members of the Fazl Ali Commission (1953)?
o: Fazl Ali, H.N. Kunzru, K.M. Panikkar
mcqs.e: It accepted language as a basis but rejected the 'one language, one state' theory.

mcqs.q: How many states and Union Territories were created by the States Reorganisation Act 1956?
mcqs.e: The old Part A, B, C and D categories of states were abolished.

mcqs.q: Which of the following states was NOT created by the States Reorganisation Act 1956?
mcqs.e: Goa was liberated from Portuguese rule in 1961 through Operation Vijay.

mcqs.q: What was the name of the military operation that liberated Goa from Portuguese control?
mcqs.e: Goa, Daman and Diu became part of India in 1961.

mcqs.q: Which amendment made Goa, Daman and Diu a Union Territory?
mcqs.e: Under the 56th Amendment (1987) Goa became a state and Daman and Diu remained a UT.

mcqs.q: Which amendment granted full statehood to Goa?
mcqs.e: Goa became a state in 1987.

mcqs.q: Which amendment made Dadra and Nagar Haveli a Union Territory?
mcqs.e: Dadra and Nagar Haveli was integrated into India in 1961.

mcqs.q: Which amendment made Puducherry a Union Territory?
mcqs.e: Puducherry was made a Union Territory in 1962.

mcqs.q: Which amendment designated Delhi as the 'National Capital Territory' (NCT)?
mcqs.e: It inserted Articles 239AA and 239AB and gave Delhi a Legislative Assembly.

mcqs.q: Article 239AB deals with:
o: President's rule in Delhi on failure of constitutional machinery
Appointment of the Lt. Governor of Delhi
Constitution of the Delhi Legislative Assembly
mcqs.e: On the Lt. Governor's report, the President can take over the administration.

mcqs.q: The limit on the size of the Council of Ministers (15% of the total strength of Lok Sabha) in Article 75(1A) was added by which amendment?
mcqs.e: The same 15% cap applies to state Assemblies, but for Delhi it is 10%.

mcqs.q: The maximum size of Delhi's Council of Ministers is what percentage of the Assembly's strength?
mcqs.e: In other states the limit is 15%.

mcqs.q: Article 371J (Hyderabad-Karnataka region) relates to which state?
mcqs.e: Added by the 98th Amendment 2012; 371A-371J: Nagaland, Assam, Manipur, Andhra (D, E), Sikkim, Mizoram, Arunachal, Goa, Karnataka.

mcqs.q: Article 371A contains special provisions for which state?
mcqs.e: 371A is Nagaland, 371B Assam and 371C Manipur.

mcqs.q: Article 371 relates to which states?
mcqs.e: 371 Maharashtra and Gujarat, 371A Nagaland, 371B Assam, 371C Manipur, and so on.

mcqs.q: Article 371F relates to which state?
mcqs.e: 371G Mizoram, 371H Arunachal Pradesh, 371I Goa.

mcqs.q: Articles 371G and 371H respectively relate to which states?
mcqs.e: 371F Sikkim, 371G Mizoram, 371H Arunachal Pradesh, 371I Goa, 371J Karnataka.

mcqs.q: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) is appointed under which Article?
mcqs.e: The President appoints the CAG; provisions are in Part V, Chapter V (Articles 148-151).

mcqs.q: The CAG is known as the:
o: Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee
mcqs.e: He is also called the friend, philosopher and guide of the PAC; it is a single-member office.

mcqs.q: To whom does the CAG submit his reports?
mcqs.e: The President causes them to be laid before Parliament; they are not binding.

mcqs.q: Article 150 deals with:
o: Form of accounts of the Union and the States
mcqs.e: Article 151 deals with the CAG's audit reports.

mcqs.q: Who was the first CAG of India?
mcqs.e: The current CAG is K. Sanjay Murthy (since November 2024).

mcqs.q: Articles 324 to 329 relating to the Election Commission are in which Part of the Constitution?
mcqs.e: Article 324 vests superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission.

mcqs.q: The Election Commission of India does NOT conduct elections to:
mcqs.e: Panchayat and municipal elections are conducted by State Election Commissions.

mcqs.q: Under Article 325, no person can be excluded from the electoral roll on grounds of:
mcqs.e: There is to be one general electoral roll for every constituency.

mcqs.q: Article 326 provides for elections on the basis of:
mcqs.e: Elections to Lok Sabha and state Assemblies are held on the basis of adult suffrage.

mcqs.q: Which Article bars interference by courts in electoral matters?
mcqs.e: Article 327 empowers Parliament and Article 328 the state legislature to make election laws.

mcqs.q: Which amendment reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years?
mcqs.e: Passed in 1988, it came into force in 1989.

mcqs.q: When did the Election Commission first become multi-member, and when permanently?
mcqs.e: It now has one Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners.

mcqs.q: How is the Chief Election Commissioner removed from office?
o: Like a Supreme Court judge (special majority in Parliament)
By a resolution of the Council of Ministers
The President can remove him on his own
mcqs.e: Other Election Commissioners can be removed by the President on the CEC's recommendation.

mcqs.q: How many Lok Sabha members must sign a motion for removal of a Supreme Court or High Court judge?
mcqs.e: In Rajya Sabha 50 members are needed; inquiry follows the Judges (Inquiry) Act 1968.

mcqs.q: On what grounds can a judge be removed?
mcqs.e: The motion must pass both Houses by special majority, after which the President removes the judge.

mcqs.q: How are decisions taken in the Election Commission?
o: By majority, the CEC having no casting power
mcqs.e: All three members have equal powers in decision-making.

mcqs.q: Who is the highest law officer of a state?
mcqs.e: The Advocate General is under Article 165; the Attorney General (Article 76) is the country's highest law officer.

mcqs.q: Which Article deals with the Attorney General of India?
mcqs.e: He has the right of audience in all courts of India and holds office during the pleasure of the President.

mcqs.q: The Finance Commission is constituted under which Article?
mcqs.e: It is a constitutional body; under Article 281 its recommendations are laid before Parliament by the President.

mcqs.q: What is the nature of the Finance Commission's recommendations?
mcqs.e: It is a quasi-judicial body with certain civil court powers, constituted every 5 years.

mcqs.q: Who is the chairman of the 16th Finance Commission?
mcqs.e: Its recommendations cover 2026-27 to 2030-31.

mcqs.q: Who was the chairman of the first Finance Commission?
mcqs.e: The first Finance Commission was set up in 1951.

mcqs.q: The GST Council is related to which Article?
mcqs.e: It is chaired by the Union Finance Minister.

mcqs.q: What is the weightage of votes of the Centre and the States in the GST Council?
mcqs.e: Decisions are taken by a three-fourths majority of weighted votes.

mcqs.q: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) is linked to which Article?
mcqs.e: Earlier there was a Special Officer; the 65th Amendment created the Commission.

mcqs.q: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST) is constituted under which Article?
mcqs.e: The 89th Amendment 2003 bifurcated the combined SC and ST Commission.

mcqs.q: Which amendment bifurcated the commission into separate commissions for SCs and STs?
mcqs.e: The 65th Amendment (1990) had replaced the Special Officer with a Commission.

mcqs.q: Which amendment gave constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC)?
mcqs.e: It is a constitutional body under Article 338B.

mcqs.q: Which Article empowers the President to appoint a commission to investigate the conditions of socially and educationally backward classes?
mcqs.e: Article 342 relates to the list of Scheduled Tribes.

mcqs.q: Article 335 relates to:
o: Claims of SCs/STs to services and posts
mcqs.e: Article 16(4) covers reservation, 16(4A) reservation in promotion, 16(4B) carry-forward of vacancies.

mcqs.q: Articles 330 to 342A, containing special provisions for certain classes, fall in which Part?
mcqs.e: These Articles protect the interests of SCs, STs and other classes.

mcqs.q: Who was the chairman of the first Backward Classes Commission (1953)?
mcqs.e: The second, the Mandal Commission (1979), was headed by B.P. Mandal.

mcqs.q: Under which Prime Minister were the Mandal Commission recommendations (27% OBC reservation) implemented?
mcqs.e: The Commission was set up in 1979 by the Janata government.

mcqs.q: The Indra Sawhney case (1992) is also known as the:
mcqs.e: The Court upheld 27% OBC reservation, excluded the creamy layer, barred reservation in promotion and capped total reservation at 50%.

mcqs.q: What ceiling on total reservation was fixed in the Indra Sawhney case?
mcqs.e: The creamy layer was excluded from reservation.

mcqs.q: The 97th Constitutional Amendment is related to:
mcqs.e: It added Part IX-B (Articles 243ZH-243ZT) and Article 43B (DPSP).

mcqs.q: Which Directive Principle, added by the 97th Amendment, deals with promotion of cooperative societies?
mcqs.e: It was added to the Directive Principles of State Policy.

mcqs.q: The system that recommends appointments and transfers of judges is called the:
mcqs.e: The collegium is not mentioned in the Constitution; it evolved through Supreme Court judgments.

mcqs.q: Which Judges case held that the CJI's advice is not binding on the President?
mcqs.e: Decided in 1981; in 1993 the advice was held to be binding.

mcqs.q: In the Second Judges case (1993), how many senior-most judges were to form the collegium along with the CJI?
mcqs.e: In the Third Judges case (1998) the number became four.

mcqs.q: According to the Third Judges case (1998), how many senior judges form the collegium along with the CJI?
mcqs.e: CJI plus four senior-most judges; their advice binds the President.

mcqs.q: In which case did the Supreme Court strike down the 99th Amendment that created the NJAC?
mcqs.e: This restored the collegium system.

mcqs.q: NITI Aayog was created by:
mcqs.e: It is neither constitutional nor statutory; it replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015, chaired by the PM.

mcqs.q: What is the full form of NITI Aayog?
mcqs.e: It replaced the Planning Commission.

mcqs.q: Who was the first chairman of the Planning Commission?
mcqs.e: The Prime Minister was the ex-officio chairman of the Planning Commission.

mcqs.q: The Central Information Commission (CIC) was created by which law, and what kind of body is it?
mcqs.e: The CIC is not in the Constitution; it was created by an Act.

mcqs.q: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) was established under which Act?
mcqs.e: It is a statutory, not a constitutional, body.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the NHRC Chairperson is correct?
o: Term of 3 years or till 70 years of age
The Prime Minister is the Chairperson
mcqs.e: The 2019 amendment reduced the term from 5 to 3 years; the NHRC cannot prosecute.

mcqs.q: What type of body is the National Commission for Women?
mcqs.e: It is not mentioned in the Constitution; it was created by an Act.

mcqs.q: Which Act gave statutory status to the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC)?
mcqs.e: The CVC was earlier an executive body (1964, Santhanam Committee).

mcqs.q: The CBI derives its powers from which law?
mcqs.e: The CBI is still a non-statutory body.

mcqs.q: Which body inquires into complaints of corruption against public servants?
mcqs.e: Created under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013, it can inquire even into the Prime Minister.

mcqs.q: The concept of Lokpal is inspired by the Ombudsman system of which country?
mcqs.e: The term 'Lokpal' was coined by L.M. Singhvi; the Administrative Reforms Commission (1966) recommended it.

mcqs.q: Apart from the Chairperson, what is the maximum number of members in the Lokpal?
mcqs.e: Half the members must be from SC, ST, OBC, minorities and women; term 5 years or till age 70.

mcqs.q: Who was the first Chairperson of the Lokpal?
mcqs.e: The current Chairperson is Justice A.M. Khanwilkar.

mcqs.q: Which was the first state to establish the institution of Lokayukta?
mcqs.e: Maharashtra set up its Lokayukta in 1971.

mcqs.q: The RTI Act 2005 originally extended to the whole of India except:
mcqs.e: It was extended there after Article 370 was abrogated in 2019.

mcqs.q: Who is referred to as the 'permanent executive'?
mcqs.e: Governments change, but civil servants remain.

mcqs.q: All India Services are related to which Article?
mcqs.e: All India Services Act 1951; IAS, IPS and IFoS are the three All India Services.

mcqs.q: To create a new All India Service, what must the Rajya Sabha do?
o: Pass a resolution by simple majority
Pass a resolution by special majority
mcqs.e: Parliament then creates the service by law (Article 312).

mcqs.q: Which Article enables the Rajya Sabha to empower Parliament to legislate on a State List subject?
mcqs.e: The Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting.

mcqs.q: All India Services reflect which feature of the Indian federal system?
mcqs.e: Their ultimate control rests with the Centre.

mcqs.q: IAS and IPS officers are recruited by which body?
mcqs.e: UPSC is covered under Articles 315-323 in Part XIV of the Constitution.

mcqs.q: Articles 315-323 relating to UPSC and State PSCs are in which Part of the Constitution?
mcqs.e: Part XIV-A contains tribunals (Articles 323A, 323B).

mcqs.q: Who appoints and who removes the members of a State Public Service Commission?
o: Appointed by the Governor, removed by the President
Appointed by the President, removed by the Governor
mcqs.e: For removal on grounds of misbehaviour, the matter is referred to the Supreme Court, whose advice is binding.

mcqs.q: On which grounds can the President directly remove a member of a Public Service Commission?
mcqs.e: Removal for misbehaviour requires an inquiry by the Supreme Court.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a Central Service and not an All India Service?
mcqs.e: IFS is a Central Service; IFoS (Forest Service) is an All India Service.

mcqs.q: Part XIV-A on tribunals was added by which amendment?
mcqs.e: It contains Articles 323A and 323B.

mcqs.q: Article 323A deals with which type of tribunals?
mcqs.e: Tribunals for other matters under Article 323B can be set up by both Parliament and state legislatures.

mcqs.q: According to the L. Chandra Kumar case (1997), an appeal against a tribunal's decision lies before:
mcqs.e: Tribunal decisions are subject to judicial review by a division bench of the High Court.

mcqs.q: The jurisdiction of the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) does NOT extend to:
o: Defence forces, Supreme Court officers and Parliament secretariat staff
mcqs.e: Defence forces have their own tribunal.

mcqs.q: Which Article gives Parliament the power to amend the Constitution?
mcqs.e: Amendments need a special majority, and some also need ratification by at least half the states.

mcqs.q: Which amendment provides 33% reservation for women in Lok Sabha and state Assemblies?
mcqs.e: Known as the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam 2023; it is for 15 years.

mcqs.q: Which Act gave statutory status to Lok Adalats?
mcqs.e: Lok Adalats are organised through NALSA under Article 39A (free legal aid).

mcqs.q: What is the nature of a Lok Adalat award?
o: Final and binding, deemed a civil court decree; no appeal
mcqs.e: The award binds both parties and no court fee is charged.

mcqs.q: Which type of cases are NOT taken up by Lok Adalats?
o: Non-compoundable offences like murder and rape
mcqs.e: Serious offences require strict punishment through regular courts.

mcqs.q: What is the nature of Lok Adalat proceedings?
mcqs.e: The aim is amicable settlement of disputes and reducing the burden of pending cases.

mcqs.q: What was the main purpose of the 2002 amendment to the Legal Services Authorities Act?
o: Giving criminal cases to Lok Adalats
Giving Lok Adalats the status of a High Court
Setting up Permanent Lok Adalats for disputes relating to public utility services
mcqs.e: It did not aim to replace regular courts or hand over criminal cases.

mcqs.q: MGNREGA implements which Directive Principle?
mcqs.e: MGNREGA guaranteed 100 days of work; the new VB-G RAM G law guarantees 125 days.

mcqs.q: Under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act 2015, juveniles of which age group can be tried as adults for heinous offences?
mcqs.e: This applies only to heinous offences.

mcqs.q: Who is called the guardian of the Constitution in India?
mcqs.e: It interprets the Constitution and exercises judicial review.

mcqs.q: Which Article provides for the appointment of an acting Chief Justice of India?
mcqs.e: 124 establishment, 125 salaries, 126 acting CJI, 127 ad hoc judges, 128 retired judges, 129 court of record, 130 seat, 131 original jurisdiction.

mcqs.q: Which Article provides for the appointment of ad hoc judges?
mcqs.e: When quorum is lacking, a High Court judge may sit temporarily; Article 128 concerns retired judges.

mcqs.q: Which Article makes the Supreme Court a 'court of record'?
mcqs.e: It also has the power to punish for its own contempt.

mcqs.q: Which Article fixes the seat of the Supreme Court (Delhi), and who can decide other places of sitting?
o: Article 130; the CJI with the President's approval
mcqs.e: Delhi is the seat; the CJI may appoint other places with the President's approval.

mcqs.q: What does Article 121 provide?
o: Courts cannot inquire into proceedings of Parliament
No discussion in Parliament on the conduct of judges
mcqs.e: Article 120 is on the language of Parliament; Article 122 bars courts from inquiring into its proceedings.

mcqs.q: What does Article 122 provide?
o: No discussion in Parliament on the conduct of judges
Courts cannot inquire into proceedings of Parliament
mcqs.e: Article 120 deals with the language used in Parliament.

mcqs.q: What is the nature of Article 136 (Special Leave Petition)?
o: A discretionary power of the Supreme Court, not a right
mcqs.e: The Supreme Court hears the matter only if it chooses to grant special leave.

mcqs.q: Under which Article is the advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court, and from where was it borrowed?
mcqs.e: Its advice to the President is not binding; it covers questions of public importance and pre-constitution matters.

mcqs.q: While appointing Supreme Court judges, whose binding advice must the President take?
mcqs.e: For High Court judges, the Governor of the state is also consulted.

mcqs.q: What kind of body is the Law Commission of India?
mcqs.e: Justice Dinesh Maheshwari chairs the 23rd Law Commission.

mcqs.q: Which dispute is excluded from the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 131?
o: Dispute between the Centre and a state
Dispute between the Centre and states on one side and other states on the other
mcqs.e: Disputes arising from pre-constitution treaties and commercial contracts are also excluded.

mcqs.q: What is the Supreme Court's jurisdiction in federal disputes?
mcqs.e: Its writ jurisdiction (Article 32) is not exclusive, as High Courts also issue writs (Article 226).

mcqs.q: What did the Supreme Court hold in the Golaknath case (1967)?
o: The Constitution has a basic structure
mcqs.e: It was later overruled in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973).

mcqs.q: The basic structure doctrine emerged from which case?
mcqs.e: Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights but cannot alter the basic structure of the Constitution.

mcqs.q: Which case held that the Constitution rests on the balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles?
mcqs.e: Harmony between the two is essential.

mcqs.q: Which Article gives the right to move the Supreme Court through writ petitions?
mcqs.e: Article 226 is for High Courts; Article 131 is original jurisdiction.

mcqs.q: What do Articles 132, 133 and 134 deal with?
o: Appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
mcqs.e: 132 constitutional cases, 133 civil cases, 134 criminal cases.

mcqs.q: Which Article provides for appeals from High Courts to the Supreme Court in civil matters?
mcqs.e: Article 134 covers criminal matters.

mcqs.q: Which Article empowers the Supreme Court to review its own judgments?
mcqs.e: For example, the Golaknath judgment was later reconsidered.

mcqs.q: Under Article 141, the law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on:
mcqs.e: Article 144 says all authorities shall act in aid of the Supreme Court.

mcqs.q: Which Article empowers the Supreme Court to pass any order for doing 'complete justice'?
mcqs.e: Under Article 144 all civil and judicial authorities shall act in aid of the Supreme Court.

mcqs.q: Which Article deals with the writ jurisdiction of High Courts?
mcqs.e: High Courts can issue writs for legal rights as well as Fundamental Rights, so their scope is wider.

mcqs.q: Which Article provides for the transfer of a judge from one High Court to another?
mcqs.e: The President transfers judges after consulting the CJI (collegium).

mcqs.q: What are the retirement ages of Supreme Court and High Court judges respectively?
mcqs.e: No minimum age is prescribed for either.

mcqs.q: What is the qualification to become a High Court judge?
o: Citizen of India with 10 years in a judicial office or 10 years as a High Court advocate
mcqs.e: For the Supreme Court: 5 years as HC judge, 10 years as HC advocate, or a distinguished jurist.

mcqs.q: In the appointment of a Supreme Court judge, who determines whether a person is a 'distinguished jurist'?
mcqs.e: No judge has so far been appointed on this ground.

mcqs.q: Who appoints a District Judge, and under which Article?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court; Article 229
mcqs.e: A District Judge must have been an advocate for at least 7 years.

mcqs.q: What is the minimum experience as an advocate required to become a District Judge?
mcqs.e: As provided under Article 233.

mcqs.q: Which Article provides for control over subordinate courts?
mcqs.e: This control is vested in the respective High Court.

mcqs.q: Who is included in the term 'judicial service' (Articles 233-237)?
o: District judges and civil judicial posts below them
mcqs.e: Executive magistrates are not part of the judicial service.

mcqs.q: Who is the highest judicial authority in civil matters in a district?
mcqs.e: The same officer is District Judge in civil matters and Sessions Judge in criminal matters.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the Sessions Court is correct?
o: It is subordinate to the Lok Adalat
Among subordinate courts it can award the highest punishment, including death
mcqs.e: The same judge is called District Judge on the civil side and Sessions Judge on the criminal side.

mcqs.q: Disputes over ownership of property and contractual obligations are heard in which court?
mcqs.e: Theft, murder and rape go to criminal courts.

mcqs.q: Which Article empowers Parliament to constitute a High Court for a Union Territory?
mcqs.e: Article 239 deals with the administration of Union Territories.

mcqs.q: Article 245 deals with what, and from which Part do Centre-State relations begin?
o: Extent of laws made by Parliament and state legislatures; Part XI
mcqs.e: Legislative relations 245-255 and administrative 256-263 (Part XI); financial 268-293 (Part XII).

mcqs.q: Article 131A was inserted by which amendment and omitted by which?
mcqs.e: Article 131A gave the Supreme Court exclusive power to decide the validity of central laws.

mcqs.q: In which Part and Articles of the Constitution are the High Courts described?
mcqs.e: The Supreme Court is in Part V, Chapter IV (Articles 124-147).

mcqs.q: What penalty can a Nyaya Panchayat impose, and can it imprison?
o: Only a small fine (a few hundred rupees); cannot imprison
mcqs.e: Nyaya Panchayats settle petty village civil and criminal disputes but cannot award imprisonment.

mcqs.q: Who first used the term 'judicial activism'?
mcqs.e: Coined in 1947; when the judiciary oversteps its limits it is called 'judicial overreach'.

mcqs.q: Who is regarded as the father of Public Interest Litigation (PIL) in India?
mcqs.e: PIL is traced to cases like Hussainara Khatoon v. State of Bihar.

mcqs.q: Which principle is relaxed in Public Interest Litigation?
mcqs.e: Any public-spirited person can approach the court on behalf of the aggrieved.

mcqs.q: What does 'locus standi' mean?
o: Only the aggrieved person can approach the court
mcqs.e: It does not apply in the case of habeas corpus.

mcqs.q: When is the writ of habeas corpus issued?
o: To make a public official perform his duty
In case of unlawful detention of a person
Against an illegal claim to a public office
mcqs.e: It literally means 'to have the body'.

mcqs.q: Which case is popularly known as the Habeas Corpus case?
mcqs.e: It was decided during the Emergency (1975-77).

mcqs.q: Which event is cited as an example of judicial activism, where the court ordered compensation?
o: 1984 Bhopal Gas Tragedy (Union Carbide, methyl isocyanate)
mcqs.e: Methyl isocyanate gas leaked from the Union Carbide plant.

mcqs.q: Which provision of the Tribunal Reforms Ordinance 2021 did the Supreme Court strike down?
mcqs.e: It was struck down on the ground of judicial independence.

mcqs.q: On which subject did the 42nd Amendment empower Parliament to set up tribunals under Article 323A?
mcqs.e: Article 323A is for administrative tribunals.

mcqs.q: What happens when a law is declared unconstitutional through judicial review?
o: It stays in force with amendments
It is sent back to Parliament
mcqs.e: For example, the 99th Amendment was declared void.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of a Lok Adalat?
mcqs.e: No appeal lies against a Lok Adalat award.

mcqs.q: Which of the following cases is generally NOT taken up by a Lok Adalat?
mcqs.e: Non-compoundable offences are outside the purview of Lok Adalats.

mcqs.q: Before becoming Chief Justice of India, B.R. Gavai was a judge of which High Court?
mcqs.e: He was elevated to the Supreme Court and later became Chief Justice of India.
